overview: Both measure solution concentration, but normality accounts for the reactive capacity (equivalents) of a solute, not just its moles.
genZNote: Molarity counts molecules. Normality counts how many 'reactive units' those molecules can actually deliver.

aspects.label: Basis of Measurement
aspects.valueA: Moles of solute per litre of solution.
aspects.valueB: Gram equivalents of solute per litre of solution.

aspects.label: Formula
aspects.valueA: Molarity (M) = moles of solute / litres of solution.
aspects.valueB: Normality (N) = Molarity x number of equivalents (valence factor).

aspects.label: Typical Use
aspects.valueA: General concentration expression across chemistry and biology.
aspects.valueB: Acid-base and redox titrations, where reactive capacity matters more than raw molecule count.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: For a monoprotic acid like HCl, Normality equals Molarity; for a diprotic acid like H2SO4, Normality is twice the Molarity.
overlay.memoryTrick: Normality = Molarity x n (number of reactive units per molecule).
overlay.commonMisconception: Molarity and Normality are not always numerically equal — they only match for compounds with an equivalence factor of exactly 1.
